beats.speaker: vane
beats.text: You always choose somewhere to stop.

beats.speaker: odessa
beats.text: Someone must keep a place for you to come back to.

beats.speaker: vane
beats.text: Then keep it close. I dislike walking home alone.

beats.speaker: vane
beats.text: The route looked shorter on the board.

beats.speaker: odessa
beats.text: It usually does when you leave out the wounded.

beats.speaker: vane
beats.text: Next time, we draw the return first.

beats.speaker: vane
beats.text: How many did we bring back?

beats.speaker: ketha
beats.text: Ask me their names first.

beats.speaker: vane
beats.text: All right. Start with the quiet ones.

beats.speaker: vane
beats.text: You were late coming off the ridge.

beats.speaker: ketha
beats.text: I had a sentence to finish.

beats.speaker: vane
beats.text: Next time use fewer explosions for punctuation.

beats.speaker: hearth
beats.text: You ask for more power before the smoke clears.

beats.speaker: brakhov
beats.text: Smoke is a sign of progress.

beats.speaker: hearth
beats.text: So is a reserve that gets the others home.

beats.speaker: hearth
beats.text: There was power left when we returned.

beats.speaker: brakhov
beats.text: A regrettable oversight.

beats.speaker: hearth
beats.text: Keep making it. I could grow fond of you.

beats.speaker: brakhov
beats.text: That wall was in the way.

beats.speaker: vale
beats.text: It was also on the invoice.

beats.speaker: brakhov
beats.text: Put a hole in the invoice.

beats.speaker: brakhov
beats.text: We returned. Close the account.

beats.speaker: vale
beats.text: Returning closes the sortie. The account has witnesses.

beats.speaker: brakhov
beats.text: Then let them witness the next one.

beats.speaker: anvil
beats.text: I can hold this angle.

beats.speaker: volt
beats.text: You cannot see the approach behind it.

beats.speaker: anvil
beats.text: Then tell me where to look before you disappear.

beats.speaker: anvil
beats.text: You stopped at the edge of the map.

beats.speaker: volt
beats.text: The edge of what we knew. Different thing.

beats.speaker: anvil
beats.text: Good. Mark the difference for the rest of us.

beats.speaker: warder
beats.text: Leave the approach clear.

beats.speaker: commando
beats.text: Clear for us, or clear for them?

beats.speaker: warder
beats.text: That is why I asked you.

beats.speaker: warder
beats.text: You left a gap in the ring.

beats.speaker: commando
beats.text: An exit. We had people outside.

beats.speaker: warder
beats.text: Keep it on the next plan. A wall should know its company.

title: A place on the manifest
setup: Vane has crossed out three descriptions of the same person. Ketha has replaced them with a name.

beats.speaker: vane
beats.text: If I write recovery asset, the quartermaster knows what to load.

beats.speaker: ketha
beats.text: If you write a name, you might remember why.

choices.label: Names first. Capabilities underneath.
choices.response: Then I can use both lists without pretending they are the same one.

choices.label: A manifest must tell us what people can do.
choices.response: Ketha leaves the name in the margin. "And this tells you who is doing it."

title: The unspent reserve
setup: Brakhov has found a power allocation with nothing assigned to it. Hearth seems pleased.

beats.speaker: hearth
beats.text: You have budgeted for nothing.

beats.speaker: brakhov
beats.text: I have budgeted for something we do not know about yet.

choices.label: Keep the reserve. Surprises do not ask permission.
choices.response: Hearth folds the page carefully. "Good. It has a job, even if we hope it never does it."

choices.label: Commit it when there is a clear opening.
choices.response: Brakhov grins. "A conditional appetite. I can work with that."

title: Damage, itemized
setup: Vale presents a form. Brakhov examines it for structural weaknesses.

beats.speaker: brakhov
beats.text: Is necessary force a number?

beats.speaker: vale
beats.text: It becomes one when someone sends the bill.

choices.label: We own the costs of what we choose to break.
choices.response: Vale adds a line for responsibility. Brakhov asks whether it has to be in ink.

choices.label: We judge the target first, the invoice second.
choices.response: Vale nods. "In that order, then. Not one instead of the other."

title: The empty chair
setup: Odessa is setting a chair beside the map table. Vane asks whether they are expecting visitors.

beats.speaker: vane
beats.text: For whoever disagrees with us.

beats.speaker: odessa
beats.text: An alarming amount of furniture, potentially.

choices.label: Keep it. I want to hear the objection.
choices.response: Odessa leaves the chair. Vane puts it where it will not block the exit.

choices.label: Hear objections, then follow the decision together.
choices.response: Vane nods. "A discussion with an ending. We will need both parts."

title: The blank corner
setup: Volt leaves a corner of the map unmarked. Anvil taps it twice.

beats.speaker: anvil
beats.text: Nothing there?

beats.speaker: volt
beats.text: Nothing we have seen. Those are different reports.

choices.label: Keep the unknown visible.
choices.response: Volt writes UNKNOWN in letters large enough to irritate everyone equally.

choices.label: Mark what we need to learn next.
choices.response: Volt draws a question mark. "A task, then. Not an answer."

title: A door without a lock
setup: Warder objects to an opening in a proposed perimeter. Commando objects to the word opening.

beats.speaker: warder
beats.text: You have drawn a weakness.

beats.speaker: commando
beats.text: I have drawn a way for our people to return.

choices.label: Every defense needs a way home.
choices.response: Warder redraws the approach with room to cover it. "Then we defend the door too."

choices.label: Keep it, but make someone responsible for it.
choices.response: Commando looks at Warder. Warder looks at the plan. The door remains.

title: The captain in the sentence
setup: Ketha is reading the wording of a proposed order aloud, very slowly.

beats.speaker: vane
beats.text: Command has determined that losses are acceptable.

beats.speaker: ketha
beats.text: You dislike the passive voice.

choices.label: Then write: I am asking you to take this risk.
choices.response: Ketha slides the page back. "Now you are in the sentence with the rest of us."

choices.label: Then write the limit, and when we turn back.
choices.response: Vane takes the pencil. "A line I can recognize in the field. Better."

title: What stays lit
setup: The conversation begins as an argument about power and becomes an argument about tomorrow.

beats.speaker: hearth
beats.text: You cannot save every spark.

beats.speaker: brakhov
beats.text: No. But I can refuse to call every spark expendable.

choices.label: Tomorrow gets a share of every plan.
choices.response: Hearth smiles without triumph. "It is a quiet shareholder. I will speak for it."

choices.label: Sometimes we spend the reserve to reach tomorrow.
choices.response: Brakhov goes quiet. "Then we should be certain it is tomorrow we are buying."

title: An honest account
setup: Vale wants an explanation for the company record. Brakhov offers three adjectives.

beats.speaker: brakhov
beats.text: None of those are an explanation.

beats.speaker: vale
beats.text: They are very good adjectives.

choices.label: Record what happened, including our mistakes.
choices.response: Vale takes a fresh sheet. "Good. The flattering version was getting difficult to reconcile."

choices.label: Record what we tried to achieve as well.
choices.response: Vale rules two columns. "Intention. Result. They can coexist without being confused."

title: The right to leave
setup: Vane has drawn a retreat route on a defense plan. Odessa studies it longer than he expected.

beats.speaker: vane
beats.text: Planning to leave already?

beats.speaker: odessa
beats.text: Planning to have a choice.

choices.label: An exit is part of every commitment.
choices.response: Odessa traces the route. "Then we should know what makes us use it."

choices.label: We name what is worth staying for.
choices.response: Vane puts down the pencil. "Specific names, please. Glory is terrible at giving directions."

title: Who gets to be certain
setup: Anvil asks for a definite answer. Volt offers a definite explanation of why there is not one.

beats.speaker: anvil
beats.text: I cannot aim at perhaps.

beats.speaker: volt
beats.text: You aim at coordinates. Perhaps tells you how much faith to put in them.

choices.label: Report uncertainty plainly. I will make the call.
choices.response: Volt nods. "Then I can stop spending half my report pretending to know more."

choices.label: Bring me a way to reduce the uncertainty.
choices.response: Anvil looks relieved. Volt looks busy. Neither calls the unknown a fact.

title: The quiet part of command
setup: Commando has returned a plan with one sentence circled. Warder reads it aloud.

beats.speaker: warder
beats.text: No one acts alone.

beats.speaker: commando
beats.text: Sometimes someone has to. The question is whether anyone knows.

choices.label: Tell us your intent. Keep room to improvise.
choices.response: Commando uncaps a pen. "That, I can report."

choices.label: Agree on the fallback before anyone moves.
choices.response: Warder adds a rendezvous. "Freedom is easier to defend when it has an address."

title: Room behind the shield
setup: Ketha has drawn a small rectangle behind Pavise on the planning board. Pavise asks what it represents.

beats.speaker: pavise
beats.text: You need a recovery position?

beats.speaker: ketha
beats.text: I need a place where being hurt does not make someone an obstruction.

choices.label: Make recovery part of the plan from the start.
choices.response: Pavise widens the rectangle. "Then the line includes this."

choices.label: Plan a moving shelter. We cannot always hold still.
choices.response: Ketha draws an arrow through the rectangle. "Then tell me before it moves."

title: The weight of an order
setup: Pavise is holding a page that has been rewritten twice. Ketha is waiting for her to put it down.

beats.speaker: pavise
beats.text: Hold until relieved. It is a clear order.

beats.speaker: ketha
beats.text: It is half an order. The other half says who comes to relieve you.

choices.label: Every holding order needs a fallback.
choices.response: Pavise reads the revised page. "This one knows what happens if we are wrong."

choices.label: I will name who is responsible for the relief.
choices.response: Ketha takes the pencil. "A name is a good start. Put the route beside it."

title: The work we left
setup: After a return recorded as partial success, Ketha sets the unfinished orders beside the roster.

beats.speaker: ketha
beats.text: We brought back a company. We did not finish the job. Both belong in the report.

beats.speaker: vane
beats.text: Put the company first. Paper has never limped off a battlefield.

beats.speaker: ketha
beats.text: And next time the people paying us will ask which part of the order we intend to keep.

choices.label: An unfinished job is a price I will pay to bring people home.
choices.response: Ketha folds the roster over the orders. "Then we tell the client before we drop. Nobody gets sold a promise we will not keep."

choices.label: We should choose smaller objectives we can actually finish.
choices.response: Vane taps the blank margin. "Leave us room to surprise you. Just stop budgeting for miracles."

choices.label: We return for unfinished work when the company is ready.
choices.response: Ketha keeps the orders. "When ready. I will remember that part too."

title: Staying is another order
setup: Their recorded return includes another contract on the same battlefield.

beats.speaker: pavise
beats.text: We held our ground and made use of it. A position is a tool, not a monument.

beats.speaker: ketha
beats.text: So is a company. Tools get checked between jobs. People should too.

beats.speaker: pavise
beats.text: Then give me a readiness report before the next order. Not an apology after it.

choices.label: Check the company before we choose another field contract.
choices.response: Ketha nods. "Names first, map second. That I can work with."

choices.label: Keep the pressure on, but give me a clear stopping condition.
choices.response: Pavise writes beneath the objective: "And this is where we stop."

title: What failure is for
setup: The defeat is in the ledger. Neither of them is willing to leave it as a single word.

beats.speaker: hearth
beats.text: I can mend a broken fitting. I cannot mend an order nobody will admit was wrong.

beats.speaker: brakhov
beats.text: Admit it, then. But do not build a shrine to it. The enemy will not wait while we confess.

beats.speaker: hearth
beats.text: I was thinking of a workbench. You can put useful things on one.

choices.label: We change the plan before asking people to try again.
choices.response: Hearth finds a clean sheet. "Good. Start with the assumption that failed us."

choices.label: We learn enough to strike back with purpose.
choices.response: Brakhov sets a weight on the old orders. "Then purpose first. Anger can carry the bags."

title: A place is not a person
setup: After a successful return, the argument turns to what success obliges them to do next.

beats.speaker: odessa
beats.text: Ground taken, company home. I would like us to become boringly good at that.

beats.speaker: vane
beats.text: A terrifying ambition. Will there be a badge?

beats.speaker: odessa
beats.text: Yes. It says everyone who left came back to be counted. We do the count before we award it.

choices.label: Make the return route part of every plan.
choices.response: Vane sketches an arrow pointing back. "There. A radical new direction."

choices.label: Keep enough freedom to leave by a different route.
choices.response: Odessa puts a second arrow beside his. "A fallback is still a plan."

title: An empty square
setup: Vale lays the last operation report beside a map with several unobserved sectors.

beats.speaker: vale
beats.text: Unknown does not mean empty. It means nobody has earned the right to draw anything there.

beats.speaker: brakhov
beats.text: And waiting will not draw it for us.

beats.speaker: vale
beats.text: No. Looking might. There is a difference between moving first and pretending you already looked.

choices.label: Tell me what we know and what we are guessing separately.
choices.response: Vale puts the pencil down. "Then I can give you an honest map."

choices.label: We can act on uncertainty if everyone understands the risk.
choices.response: Brakhov nods. "A risk we name is an order we can argue with. Better than a surprise."

title: Room in the schedule
setup: The return ledger includes wounded company members. Odessa and Hearth review the next preparations.

beats.speaker: odessa
beats.text: Recovery is on the roster. It needs to be on the schedule.

beats.speaker: hearth
beats.text: The schedule currently says soon in three different places. I can build many things. Soon is not one of them.

beats.speaker: odessa
beats.text: Give me a decision I can tell the wounded. Waiting is harder when nobody admits it is waiting.

choices.label: Recovery comes before another ambitious sortie.
choices.response: Hearth crosses out one soon. "A rare material. An actual priority."

choices.label: Prepare a smaller operation around who is ready.
choices.response: Odessa circles the available names. "Then we plan for these people, not the people we wish were well."
